basis: Adds separately labelled processed histology references and their specimen/MRI limitations to muscle-interface teaching; no report checklist, report template, structure extent or approval is changed.

protocol: Record indication and dates of biopsy, TURBT, intravesical and systemic treatment; primary local-staging MRI is preferably before TURBT.
Assess moderate bladder distension, coverage, motion and susceptibility on each sequence. Record which lesion interfaces are assessable.
Use acquired small-field T2 in appropriate planes, high-b DWI with ADC and an actual early dynamic contrast series; late enhancement is not a substitute for DCE.

checklist.label: Lesion map
checklist.detail: Number lesions and record wall location and size.

checklist.label: Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe papillary/sessile form, stalk and underlying wall.

checklist.label: Muscle interface
checklist.detail: Trace the muscle and inner-layer/stalk morphology in more than one plane; assess bladder neck, UVJ and diverticula explicitly.

checklist.label: Functional sequences
checklist.detail: Record each functional category, quality and discordance; apply optimal-quality DWI priority for 4–5, then DCE, using the original combination algorithm.

checklist.label: Beyond bladder
checklist.detail: Assess perivesical spread, adjacent organs, ureters and nodes.

measurements.name: Tumour size
measurements.method: Record maximum dimension and base/wall relationship.
measurements.pitfall: An underfilled bladder can mimic thickening.

measurements.name: Nodal assessment
measurements.method: Measure short axis by named station and describe morphology.
measurements.pitfall: MRI nodal staging has limitations for microscopic disease.

classification.name: VI-RADS
classification.applicability: Lesion-specific baseline muscle-invasion assessment on suitable MRI. Record quality and treatment confounders; do not substitute baseline categories for a treatment-response framework.
classification.summary: Scores 1–5 express increasing likelihood of muscle invasion; combine T2 structure with diffusion and contrast findings using the published algorithm.

pitfalls: Scoring on an underdistended bladder. Wall thickening from an empty or non-distended bladder mimics tumour and disrupts the muscularis propria assessment.
Applying a majority vote or selecting the worst-looking sequence regardless of quality. Record each category and use the published hierarchy and combinations.
Missing early enhancement because the dynamic series was not truly early. Delayed post-contrast imaging cannot distinguish focal early enhancement from generalised bladder wall enhancement.
Assuming a fixed waiting interval after treatment restores baseline scoring reliability. Describe the intervention, dates and persistent confounders.
Stopping at the VI-RADS category without staging locoregional and upper-tract disease when the category is 4 or 5.
At the ureterovesical junction and bladder neck, normal openings and prostate protrusion complicate the muscle interface. Review the anatomy in more than one plane.
A diverticulum may lack muscularis propria; do not force the ordinary muscle-interface rule onto absent muscle.
Baseline VI-RADS does not establish treatment response, exclude CIS or prove histological grade.
Do not use a universal ADC cutoff when acquisition, scaling or physical units are unverified.
MRI cannot exclude flat carcinoma in situ or microscopic perivesical invasion.
Node size and enhancement do not prove metastatic disease; record station and degree of suspicion.
impression_prompts: State the index lesion’s site, size and VI-RADS score with sequence evidence.
Describe any extravesical or adjacent-organ invasion.
Report nodes, obstruction and technical/post-treatment limitations.

steps.label: Lesion inventory
steps.detail: Record treatment context and sequence quality, then number lesions and describe location, dimensions, base, inner layer and stalk.
findings: Single [papillary / sessile] tumour on the [left lateral wall], __ mm, [with / without] a stalk.
steps.look: Small-field T2 in three planes with a well-distended bladder.

steps.label: T2 muscle interface
steps.detail: Assess the continuity of the low-T2 muscular layer beneath each lesion.
findings: Stalk/thickened inner layer and preserved muscle: record the full structural criteria, including size, before assigning category 1 or 2.
Category 2 morphology absent but no clear muscle disruption: structural category 3.
Loss of the low-signal muscle line beneath the tumour (T2 score 4).
Tumour extends through the muscle into the perivesical fat (T2 score 5).
steps.look: High-resolution T2 perpendicular to the tumour base.
steps.tip: Stalk and inner-layer findings support the structural assessment; they do not prove histology. Review the UVJ, neck and any diverticulum. The Jansen figures are independent processed tissue references: tumour and muscularis propria are separately outlined, with specimen 1 source-reported as Ta. They are not registered to the MRI examples and cannot justify an MRI score or prove muscle invasion.
steps.anatomy_note: The current gross anatomy and MRI tumour-cell models do not resolve every fine wall layer. Published histology renderings supply separate tissue context; deliberately blurred tissue in Figure 6 is not absent anatomy.

steps.label: Diffusion
steps.detail: Assess DWI/ADC quality and restriction extending into muscle or perivesical tissue, retaining discordance.
findings: Restricted diffusion confined to the tumour with a low-signal stalk (DWI score 1–2).
Restricted diffusion extends focally into the muscular layer (DWI score 4).
Restricted diffusion extends to the perivesical fat (DWI score 5).
steps.look: High-b-value DWI and ADC matched to the T2 plane.
steps.tip: For categories 4–5, DWI is dominant when quality is optimal; DCE is next. T2 guides the first pass, especially 1–3. Use the original combination rules.

steps.label: Dynamic contrast enhancement
steps.detail: Assess the early enhancement pattern at the tumour base.
findings: Early enhancement confined to the inner layer (DCE score 1–2).
Early enhancement extends focally into the muscular layer (DCE score 4).
Early enhancement extends through the wall into perivesical fat (DCE score 5).
steps.look: Early dynamic phase at the tumour–muscle interface.

steps.label: Extent and VI-RADS
steps.detail: Apply the original sequence-combination rules; state quality, treatment limits and lesion-specific evidence. Describe visible extension, obstruction and suspicious nodes separately.
findings: Overall VI-RADS 5 with extravesical extension to the [ ].
Tumour at the [left] ureteric orifice with hydroureteronephrosis.
steps.look: Integrate the three sequences; review the ureteric orifices, prostate or uterus, and pelvic nodes.
steps.tip: VI-RADS is muscle-invasion likelihood, not histology, treatment selection or microscopic staging. Record any unassessed anatomy.

spatial_model.instructions: Drag to rotate; choose a reporting landmark and move the section plane. Relate mucosal surface, muscular wall and perivesical tissue; invasion assessment needs multiplanar T2, diffusion and enhancement.

reader_tissue_figures.alt: Complete original four-panel human bladder histology figure, with original H&E tissue in panel a and separate annotation/training preparations in panels b–d.
reader_tissue_figures.caption: Published H&E tissue example (a): urothelium, lamina propria and red blood cells are annotated by the authors’ pathologist in (b). Panels (c) and (d) remove unlabelled regions for training; they are processed evidence, not complete tissue. Black/unlabelled does not mean absent anatomy. This specimen is separate from the linked TCGA MRI and HRA reference models.
reader_tissue_figures.limits: Complete published figure, not whole-slide source resolution or a full-thickness wall section. Only selected regions have pathologist labels; unlabelled tissue remains unknown. Muscularis propria, muscularis mucosae, complete serosa/adventitia and native3D layer extent are not established. No MRI correspondence, current diagnosis or complete reporting-anatomy approval is granted.

reader_tissue_figures.caption: Original Figure 1: right, digitized en-bloc tissue with the authors’ tumour outlines in red and muscularis propria in orange; left, the annotation workstation photograph. The specimen number is not stated. Labels are publication evidence, not a new pathology reading.
reader_tissue_figures.alt: Original Figure 1: right, digitized en-bloc tissue with the authors’ tumour outlines in red and muscularis propria in orange; left, the annotation workstation photograph. The specimen number is not stated. Labels are publication evidence, not a new pathology reading.
reader_tissue_figures.limits: Formalin fixation, paraffin embedding, sectioning, mounting and staining alter the tissue. The authors aligned sections by rigid, affine and nonrigid B-spline transformations; registration was assessed qualitatively. Excluded sections could be replaced by duplicate neighbours, and only portions of tumour blocks were sectioned. Whole-slide sampling reported as 0.5 micrometres/pixel does not describe the resolution of these published bitmaps. Native slide arrays, masks and aligned volumes are not publicly supplied. No whole-wall or microscopic invasion validation, native 3D geometry, calibrated independent tissue measurement, MRI correspondence, current diagnosis or VI-RADS category is established.
